newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas seen up after late Thursday deals.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas seen up after late Thursday deals.

text.p: IPE natural gas prices were expected to rise again on Friday after firm business was concluded on the physical market after Thursday's IPE close, traders and brokers said.

IPE prices strengthened on Wednesday on good volumes as large players came into the market in what brokers said was partly an effort to expoit the relative illiquidity of the IPE market to push up levels on small volumes.
Front month May natural gas pushed higher on Thursday to close at 10.175 pence per therm , while the summer months gained slightly.
After the close, physical markets gained some more.

"A couple of parties were on the warpath yesterday after the IPE closed," one broker said, adding that the fourth quarter of this year stood at around 13.5 pence on the physical market, with the first quarter of next year worth around 15.7-15.8 pence.

The broker anticipated gains of somewhere around 0.1 pence per therm across the board, although he echoed the sentiment of others who feel the fundamental supply/demand situation does not warrant substantial further gains.
Physical markets were firmer because traders who failed to win storage capacity in Transco's annual tender had to scramble for gas, traders said.
Transco forecast slightly stronger demand for gas on Friday, at 55 percent of peak demand, compared to 49 percent on Wednesday. But temperatures were expected to be around seasonal norms.
